title: Colts’ Daniel Jones will be ‘full go’ at camp: ‘There’s nothing I can’t do’
content:
Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones will be a full participant in training camp, he announced Monday on The Pat McAfee Show. After not participating in 11-on-11 drills during spring practice, Jones told McAfee, “There’s nothing that I can’t do,” now that he’s more than seven months removed from rupturing his right Achilles tendon and undergoing surgery.

“The plan is to be back in 11-on-11, full team drills Wednesday when we start up practice,” Jones said, confirming the Colts’ plan from the spring. “(I’ll) be out there with the guys. Excited to get back rolling. … Rehab’s been good to this point. Still some work to do as we get ready for Week 1, but feeling good with where I am. … I’m gonna be a full go to start camp.”

Last year, Jones joined the Colts on a one-year, $14 million deal and won the starting job over 2023 No. 4 pick Anthony Richardson Sr. in training camp. Jones started the 2025 season on fire and was playing arguably the best football of his career until he fractured his left fibula, which he played through, before then tearing his right Achilles tendon in December. Jones threw 19 touchdowns against eight interceptions in 13 games. He also tallied five rushing TDs.

The Colts re-signed Jones in March on a two-year, $88 million deal that included $50 million guaranteed at signing. The 29-year-old is entering his eighth NFL season, but he’s only made it through one without missing games due to injury or being benched. Fittingly, that lone season was when Jones led the New York Giants to the playoffs in 2022, ending a five-year postseason drought. Now, the Colts hope Jones, with his repaired Achilles tendon, can help them end their own five-year playoff drought.

“I think you’re constantly evaluating. It’s hard not to compare (yourself to your pre-injury form),” Jones said. “I think I’m in a really good spot. Like I said, I can do everything. There’s nothing I can’t do. I think there’s still that last little bit that you’re working to get back, but I feel good.”

Jones said he’s confident he can clear his last few physical and mental hurdles before the Colts’ season opener against the Baltimore Ravens on Sept. 13. It remains to be seen if he’ll play in any of the Colts’ preseason games, but coach Shane Steichen praised his QB for his diligence amid his lengthy rehab.

“He looks great,” Steichen said in an ESPN interview Saturday. “He’s attacked the rehab process as good as it gets. He’s in that building all spring from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. He’s put in the work. He got some good reps during OTAs doing seven-on-seven, but he’ll be a full participant when we start (training camp) next week and get into the team drills. I know he’s looking forward to that, and he’s ready to go.”
